title: Voice for Animals (Independent Office of Animal Welfare) Bill 2013

speeches.speaker: Adam Bandt
speeches.brief: Introduced the Voice for Animals (Independent Office of Animal Welfare) Bill 2013, noting more than 500,000 Australian cattle are sent to Indonesian slaughterhouses each year, and contrasted the government's five-month rollout of the ESCAS export scheme after the 2011 cruelty scandal with two and a half years of inaction on the promised animal welfare office, which the Parliamentary Budget Office costed at just $0.5 million.

speeches.speaker: Sid Sidebottom
speeches.brief: Opposed the bill, saying the government had substantially strengthened animal welfare standards through ESCAS, national guidelines and international engagement. Reported that an ALP working group had completed a model for an office of animal welfare, but said constitutional, legal, policy and consultation issues required further consideration.

speeches.speaker: Barry Haase
speeches.brief: Opposed the bill, arguing that it would contribute to shutting down live exports and harm pastoral communities across Northern Australia. Said local slaughter and boxed beef exports were not economically viable for relevant markets, and that the live export ban had worsened conditions for cattle and producers.

speeches.speaker: Graham Perrett
speeches.brief: Supported the aim of improving animal welfare but said the bill overlooked Australia's federal structure and the economic realities of northern cattle production. Reported that the government was considering an announcement on an office of animal welfare and argued that any arrangement would require cooperation with the states.
